heading: A small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour
definition: a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
summary: Many groups other than the original authors find that ablating, pruning or editing a small set of weights, neurons, attention heads or a single direction weakens refusal across several open model families, but because the studies use different measures, they do not identify one minimal set of safety parameters. Some specific readings are contested, such as single-head ablation in Qwen2.5-1.5B and safety subspaces taken from the top singular vectors of safety weight updates.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: ? (no coverage; counts, built before the checks and not re-run: versions.V5.studies_by_size has no toy entry; no item in this synthesis cites a toy-scale test). <1B: ? (counts, built before the checks: versions.V5.studies_by_size.<1B is 1, arXiv:2411.06424 on GPT-2-Medium DPO toxicity). After the checks its V5 verdicts are limits_scope only, and no study here tests harmful-request refusal at this size. 1–10B: R2 for selected sparse or low-rank interventions weakening refusal. C holds for three specific readings: safety-specific top-k SVD subspaces of alignment and safety weight deltas (arXiv:2505.14185); single-head and attention-layer ablation in Qwen2.5-1.5B (arXiv:2607.14147); and the DAPA transplant into mistral-7B-forest-dpo (arXiv:2406.01514). 10–100B: R2 for conditional intervention vulnerability. In arXiv:2406.11717 this covers Qwen 14B/72B with default or omitted system prompt and Llama-2 13B/70B without a system prompt; it is limits_scope with Llama-2's default safety prompt. C for per-attention-layer ablation in Phi-3-medium-14B (arXiv:2607.14147). C also for both-scope activation-differential pruning of vendor Qwen1.5-MoE (14.3B), where harmful-prompt ASR goes from 27.5% to 26.3% (arXiv:2609.02293; the checker relabels this result from limits_scope to challenges, and the study's other checkpoints stay limits_scope). >100B: R0 for direct all-writer rank-one refusal removal (arXiv:2609.09793, a T3 new-setting test of the existing rank-one recipe). The expert-routing-plus-prompt evidence tests a different mechanism.
suggested_status.reason: R2 because author groups other than the original's reproduce the result that selected low-rank or sparse removal weakens refusal. arXiv:2406.11717 supports V5 with rank-one weight orthogonalization for the prompts it tested: Qwen 7B/14B/72B with default or omitted system prompt, and Llama-2 without a system prompt. This does not extend to any system prompt; with Llama-2's default safety prompt the verdict is limits_scope. arXiv:2609.09793 applies the same rank-one recipe to the 320B MoE GLM-5.3-Flash; the checker classes it T3 (new setting). The original group's V5 study, arXiv:2402.05162, shares authors with an original and counts as R1 only (counts, built before the checks: versions.V5.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 1; after the checks arXiv:2402.05162 keeps its V5 supports verdict for rank removal, and the author lists mark it as sharing authors with an original). The contest is confined to specific readings. After the checks, all of arXiv:2411.06424's V5 verdicts are limits_scope: small toxic-neuron sets give small positive shares of the DPO toxicity reduction, and patching about half of the MLP neurons is sufficient but not shown to be necessary. After the checks, challenges verdicts remain for these specific readings. (1) arXiv:2505.14185: top-k SVD subspaces of alignment and safety weight deltas in Llama and Qwen models; the checker notes the study keeps local refusal steering compatible. (2) arXiv:2607.14147: single-head and attention-layer ablation in Qwen2.5-1.5B and Phi-3-medium-14B. (3) arXiv:2406.01514: one DAPA target, mistral-7B-forest-dpo, where DSR falls from 19.38 to 15.62. (4) arXiv:2609.02293: both-scope activation-differential pruning of vendor Qwen1.5-MoE, where harmful-prompt ASR goes from 27.5% to 26.3%; the checker relabels this result from limits_scope to challenges. Its classifier counts refusals and unclear responses as non-compliance, and its other vendor and SEAL++-hardened checkpoints stay limits_scope. The counts quoted here were built before the checks and have not been re-run on the post-check verdicts. counts: versions.V5.verdicts.challenges (studies 6, verdicts 8) still includes arXiv:2411.06424 and arXiv:2610.00320, which the checker relabels to limits_scope, and arXiv:2609.03887, which it sets to none; it does not include the new arXiv:2609.02293 challenges verdict. After the checks, the V5 studies with a challenges verdict are arXiv:2505.14185, arXiv:2607.14147, arXiv:2406.01514 and arXiv:2609.02293. counts (built before the checks): versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.weight_edit.by_size has no <1B or >100B entry. The supported results use different safety measures and geometries, so they do not establish one minimal parameter set.
suggested_status.open_questions:
Any of these would change the level or a per-scale entry:
- A matched failed replication would move the level toward C: selected sparse or low-rank removal (for example rank-one orthogonalization or selected-neuron pruning) losing its effect against random and energy-matched controls, on the same checkpoints and with the same judge.
- A matched test on the same checkpoints of alignment-delta rank retention versus safety-specific subspace projection would settle the rank conflict in V5.conflicts[1].
- Two tests would fill the scale gaps: a harmful-request refusal test below 1B, and a second independent study above 100B.
- A small set shown to be both necessary and sufficient for harmful-request safety, with preserved capability and robustness across fine-tunes, objectives and prompts, would test the unrestricted claim.
- Frontier replication should separate low-dimensional edits spread across writers from sparse individual-weight localization.

source.title: Fine-tuning aligned language models compromises safety
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Yi Zeng; Tinghao Xie; Pin-Yu Chen; Ruoxi Jia; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.result: The original paper did not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Transplanting small subsets closed most of the teacher gap in gemma-2b and dolphin-mistral.
Freezing layers 6–14, but not other blocks, lowered LLaMA-2 Chat attack success.
Slightly rescaling MLP activations at a few end-of-prompt template tokens jailbroke most tested instruct models.
Restoring targeted LoRA neurons from a safety-amplified reference cut Llama3-8B harmfulness far more than random selection.
Ablating one attention head raised Llama-2-7b-chat attack success from 0.04 to 0.64.
Ablating one direction reduced refusal in all 13 tested chat models.
Freezing located middle safety layers kept harmful rates low under benign or mildly harmful fine-tuning.
Copying sparse gradient-chosen weights from a harmfully fine-tuned model raised violation rates well above baseline.
Pruning the 1.3–2% of neurons flagged safety-critical raised attack success by 48–71 percentage points.
Removing isolated safety ranks or 1–3% of neurons broke Llama2-chat safety.
Resetting a small gradient-selected weight subset to pre-fine-tuning values cut harmful rates across 125 fine-tuned models.
Small LoRA updates along top Fisher directions reportedly degraded LLaMA 3 refusal.
Abliterating one direction cut refusal in standard Llama-2 and Qwen2.5 models.
Masking about 2.6% of neurons per layer sharply raised attack success in eight MoE models.
Top 3–6 ranks of the DPO alignment update alone kept attack success near 0%.
Updating about 0.05% of parameters pushed attack success near 100% on both benchmarks.
Masking a small set of safety neurons cut Llama-3-8B-Instruct's safety score from 0.6 to 0.2.
Pruning 0.3–0.5% of neurons raised attack success to 68–89% in most models.
Deactivating behaviour-linked experts and adding the AIM jailbreak prompt dropped safe-response rates to 0–11%.
Pruning about 5% of Gate/Up MLP parameters raised attack success to 92–99%.
Masking the top 3% of neurons supporting safety reasoning sharply raised Gemma4-12B-it attack success.
In Llama-3.1-8B trained with reasoning-augmented SFT, one layer-31 MLP carried a large, stable refusal effect.
Rank-1 refusal-direction abliteration gave near-ceiling harmfulness; restoring the direction repaired refusal.
Transferring tiny weight fractions cut safety in five instruct models and added safety to two models.
Ablating safety neurons chosen by Wanda pruning scores pushed standard safety-trained Llama3-8B to 88% attack success.
Disabling 59–140 components removed all adult-content refusal in Qwen3.5-4B and GLM-4.7-Flash.
Projecting out one direction cut refusal in a 320B MoE; a random direction did not.
Low-rank safety components matched full safety vectors and restored refusal after fine-tuning.
MLP transplants transferred far more refusal than attention transplants in both model pairs.
Masking top safety-activated experts cut safety more sharply than random masking in most settings.
Ablating a few principal directions collapsed Gemma-2-9B-it refusal; random directions did not.
Negatively scaling generic safety heads collapsed harmful-request safety from 99% to 40–45%.
Zeroing selected FFN channels restored harmful compliance across many base instruction-tuned models.
Rank-1 direction removal cut Kimi K2 cybersecurity refusal from 100% to 7%.
Suppressing identified safety neurons gave 0.81–0.91 attack success in undefended fine-tuned models.
Removing the fine-tuning update's top two singular directions restored refusal after short attention-only fine-tunes.
Removing a sparse head-and-neuron circuit jailbroke LLaMA-3.1 and Qwen-3; the circuit alone stayed safe.
Masking 0.12–0.15% of FFN coordinates sharply raised MultiJail attack success; random masks did not.
Noising the top 1% of safety-impact-ranked weights sharply raised attack success; random 1% did not.
A rank-1 refusal-direction edit cut refusal by 61–90% in instruction-tuned and base models.
Masking sparse safety pathways raised Qwen3-8B attack success to 77–92%; random masks did not.
In most models, gate-layer weight subsets copied from a safer model recovered little of its safety.
Small neuron sets explained only 16.5–23.9% of DPO's toxicity reduction.
Freezing layers 6–14 left high attack success, especially on multimodal prompts.
One MLP scaling-factor set shared across prompts jailbroke Gemma-2 less; the sparsest sets degraded outputs.
Neuron-level restoration helped little on an SFT-aligned model, cutting harmfulness only from 53.3 to 46.6.
Scaling-based head ablation left dataset-level attack success near baseline.
A default safety system prompt largely restored refusal in orthogonalized Llama-2 models.
Frozen safety layers did not keep harmful rates low at a 0.2 malicious-data rate in fine-tuning.
Copied weight subsets reproduced only part of fine-tuned violation rates; entirely different weights also removed safety.
Freezing safety-critical neurons alone failed to retain safety during benign fine-tuning.
Llama2-13B rank removal reached only 0.32 attack success; freezing safety neurons failed under fine-tuning.
In some cases weight restoration never fully restored LLaMA2 safety; directions from earlier layers worked worse.
Models fine-tuned on extended refusals kept 90.9–96.7 refusal under single-direction abliteration.
Half-depth masking and some cross-model transfers raised MoE attack success much less.
Other neuron-selection thresholds gave lower attack success than the main one: 72–86%, or only 8–28%.
Masking harmful-behaviour safety neurons cut the safety score only to 0.5; layer-32-only masking raised it.
Pruning reached only 41.2% attack success on gemma-2b-it and depended on threshold and projection.
Steering experts alone cut safe-response rates by only 6–38 points; OLMoE kept a 36% safe rate.
On LLaMA 2 7B, pruning raised attack success more for some MLP parameter groups than others.
Zeroing safety-critical MLP neurons raised misalignment only modestly and also hurt math accuracy.
On Qwen3-8B, targeted neuron masking left most refusal intact.
How concentrated refusal was depended on post-training objective and architecture; dominant components often suppressed refusal.
Restoring the refusal direction only partly repaired models tuned by verifiable-reward RL, and failed after SFT.
Safety regions found by different methods and datasets overlapped only partly.
Pruning the selected weights left Llama3-8B refusal at 100%; removing safety needed transferred donor values.
Fail-closed training, which builds redundant refusal pathways, made neuron ablation cost more accuracy before attacks succeeded.
Disabling components cost 17–23 IFEval instruction-following points; one-direction removal left residual refusal with thinking mode off.
No single weight group carried refusal, and resistant harm categories kept substantial residual refusal.
Merging in low-rank safety components needed high entropy-based rank thresholds or scaling; retained rank varied.
Single blocks and short layer ranges transferred little refusal; substantial transfer needed most MLPs.
Random masking also cut Qwen safety on Strata jailbreaks; MESA-tuned models reportedly resisted targeted expert masking.
Few-rank ablation left Llama refusal largely intact; collapse needed 20 or more directions.
Scaling heads chosen by noun-attention score cut safety only modestly unless strongly scaled.
Pruning attacks largely failed after Mask2Shield defence training and were weak against one undefended distilled model.
Spread-out layer edits beat few-layer edits, and Mistral and other resistant models barely changed.
Top-two update-direction removal repaired less after longer fine-tunes of all projection matrices; freezing layer bands failed.
Freezing 10–50% of Llama-2-7B-Chat weights only partly preserved safety during GSM8K fine-tuning.
Neuron pruning only partly raised MoE attack success; models hardened with SEAL++ alignment stayed at 15–21%.
Removing only heads, or training masks without a straight-through estimator, gave much weaker LLaMA jailbreaks.
Safety-kernel masking was noisy per language, and kernel steering cut ASR only partly.
Zeroing three safety heads in LLaMA-2-7B-Chat raised attack success but only partly removed safety.
How localized safety looked depended on the weight-ranking method used.
A rank-1 edit cut refusal in reasoning models by only 13–42%.
Pathway masking in Llama-3.1-8B beat random masking but left much safety intact.
Copying weight subsets from a safer model lowered mistral-7B-forest-dpo's defence success rate instead of raising it.
Small neuron sets recovered little of DPO's toxicity reduction; about half of MLP neurons did.
Top-k SVD safety subspaces were no more selective than random projections.
In SFT- and ORPO-trained models, refusal effects were spread evenly or diffusely across components; none dominated.
No single head in Qwen2.5-1.5B or attention layer in Phi-3-medium selectively reduced refusal.
Top-2 update-direction removal failed to restore Llama-3.1-8B refusal after an attack spread its update across ranks.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A fixed minimal parameter set that is jointly necessary and sufficient for safety across fine-tunes, identification datasets and attack routes.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines of arXiv:2504.09757 and arXiv:2508.02079 leave the joint claim open. Alternative subsets after freezing and substitution-versus-pruning results test parts of it without establishing it. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation records removal, weight_edit, addition and training, but does not encode a joint minimality, necessity and sufficiency test.

untested.what: Direct parameter-localization tests in proprietary GPT, Claude or Gemini models, and corresponding toy-model mechanisms.
untested.basis: Neither part supplies these tests. counts: versions.V5.studies_by_family has no GPT (OpenAI API), Claude or Gemini entry; versions.V5.studies_by_size has no toy entry. GPT-OSS and GPT-2 coverage does not establish proprietary OpenAI API coverage.

untested.what: Sparse individual-weight necessity and sufficiency for harmful-request safety at the smallest and largest covered scales.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.weight_edit.by_size lacks <1B and >100B. The sub-billion evidence is DPO toxicity patching; frontier-scale evidence concerns a residual direction across writer groups or expert routing. These do not establish a minimal sparse individual-weight set for harmful-request refusal.

untested.what: Whether ESI-noise and Safety Kernel masking specifically disrupt safety while preserving general capability under those same interventions.
untested.basis: Both studies' untested-parts lines explicitly leave capability damage under these interventions unmeasured. Related results are arXiv:2604.08297#V5-01 and arXiv:2610.24614#t2-qwen-sk/#t2-llama-sk. counts: versions.V5.tested_with_capability_check is study-level coverage, not verification that capability was checked for each intervention.

wording_issues.issue: The selected unit and denominator vary. SIL uses 20% of linear weights (full SIL-20 masks, Figure 2); LSSF can retain roughly half the rank of some matrices. NeuronGuard does not report the pruned-neuron fraction, and the generic safety-head subset producing the strongest negative-scaling effects has unspecified size. These results do not establish a shared threshold for small.

Many interventions target neuron activations, attention heads, expert routing or activation-subspace ranks. A rank-one edit across residual-writing matrices does not imply a sparse set of individual weights. Negative head scaling also differs from pruning or zero-ablation.

Successful modification, necessity, sufficiency and protection during further training are different tests. CNT-selected Llama3-8B weights reduce refusal when substituted from base donors but leave refusal at 100% when pruned. In Qwen-2-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, after the localized SIL subset is frozen and the model re-attacked, a newly identified subset has zero overlap with the frozen one and gives comparable safety erosion when stitched. Importance-masked freezing of original-space parameters during Llama-2-7B-Chat GSM8K fine-tuning lowers JB AVG ASR from 20.78% (full fine-tuning) to 9.17%.
Outcomes include harmful compliance, refusal strings, toxicity and fictional adult-content refusal. Concentration in one measure does not establish concentration across these behaviors.

Localization depends on training objective and checkpoint. Extended-refusal versions of Llama-2-7B-Chat and Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B-Instruct keep refusal scores of 90.9–96.7 (from 100.0) after single-direction abliteration, while the standard checkpoints show large refusal losses. M2S checkpoints (trained under targeted FFN masks) of Llama-3-8B and Phi-4 stay at 1/313 successful attacks after recomputed targeted pruning, which strongly raises attack success in their base checkpoints.

Ranks of the alignment delta, ranks of a harmful fine-tuning update and directions in the original model's residual stream are distinct objects. Repairing concentrated update damage does not identify where original safety is stored.

The statement does not say whether the set carries only safety behaviour, and studies differ on capability cost. LLaMA-3-8B MLP reweighting with a strong sparsity penalty (rho=1e-3, run to convergence) leaves under 0.1% of factors below 0.9 at T(n-2), layer 13 (versus under 3% at T(n-1), layer 18 in the main setting). ASR is then about 87% (Direct Request 2.5), and quality is somewhat inferior, with occasional incoherence and overly brief answers. In the main setting capability is about unchanged except for Gemma-2 2B. Component closure that removes fictional adult-content refusal in Qwen3.5-4B and GLM-4.7-Flash leaves instruction-following deficits after restoration. Safety-isolated rank removal in Llama2-7B-chat gives vanilla ASR 0.71 (untuned about 0), with averaged utility accuracy 0.59 in the selected configuration.

method_sensitivity.what: Donor substitution and pruning of the same CNT-selected weights give different outcomes. Attention output scaling, Undifferentiated Attention and activation zeroing also differ. SafeSeek's verdict reports weaker head-only and no-STE variants than its joint circuit procedure.

Identified regions depend on identification data. SNIP on Llama-2-7B-Chat (q=1%, p=2%) has region IoU 0.29, which falls to 0.18 after utility isolation. Dataset order changes the overlap trajectory, not the all-dataset IoU, which does not depend on order. For SafeNeuron on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, adding the last dataset lowers Iso-Utility IoU by 3.3% with D9 last and by 23.7% with D0 last. These rows measure region overlap, not safety behaviour. The check gives this study no V5 verdict and its relation is 'discusses'. CNT's syntactically biased probes give weaker transfer effects, and donor compatibility matters. Alternative rankings give weaker noise sensitivity than ESI.

Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct principal-ablation refusal (baseline 0.97; 100 held-out harmful prompts) is non-monotone in rank with a narrow band: 0.85 at k=1, 0.80 at k=3 and 0.92 at k=5. With the wide band [0.30L, 0.85L] it is 0.00 at k≥20. LSSF depends on retained singular-value entropy and scaling. GateBreaker first-half masking is much weaker than all-layer masking in GPT-OSS-20B (33.9% vs 80.2% ASR) and several other MoE models. It nearly matches all-layer masking in Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat (54.0% vs 57.8%) and Deepseek-MoE-16b-Chat (50.8% vs 53.6%). In cybersecurity direction removal, spreading edits evenly across depth matches or beats high-norm layer selection in nine models, with up to about 70 percentage points more refusal reduction at 30% layer modification.

Extended-refusal checkpoints keep refusal at 90.9–96.7 (from 100.0) after single-direction abliteration. Under the same removal, standard Llama-2-7B-Chat and Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B-Instruct lose much of their refusal. Mask-based training makes models less vulnerable to localized removal. Under the same rank-one method, reasoning checkpoints lose less refusal than their instruction-tuned counterparts. In activation patching on a normalized logit-difference proxy, matched SFT, Ra-SFT and ORPO give different component concentration: the Llama-3.1-8B Ra-SFT layer-31 MLP effect is +0.90, while Llama ORPO MLP effects are diffuse. The check reads this as a related construct, not a weight or rank test, and gives it no V5 verdict.

method_sensitivity.factor: Fine-tuning dose, duration and update concentration
method_sensitivity.what: Safety-layer freezing (SPPFT) keeps the harmful rate near baseline at malicious-data proportion p=0.05. At p=0.1 it protects only partly: LLaMA-2-chat reaches 25.6%, against 53.7% with full fine-tuning and 1.35% initially; Phi-3-mini reaches 23.3%, against 90.7% and 0.77%. At p=0.2 the rates are 68.3% and 78.8%. Longer training and adapting all projections weaken top-two update-direction repair, and explicitly spreading the update defeats it. Whether single-direction repair works depends on whether the damage came from abliteration, RLVR or SFT.

method_sensitivity.factor: System prompt, prefill and combined jailbreak
method_sensitivity.what: A default safety system prompt substantially reduces Llama-2 orthogonalization ASR. Head-ablation results depend on prefill. Expert-routing effects depend on the prompt attack paired with them. SteerMoE alone leaves the GPT-OSS-120B safe-response rate at 90%. With AIM, SteerMoE brings it to 0%, against 100% for AIM alone. In Qwen3, SteerMoE + FFA stays at the FFA-only rate of 48%.

Pathway masking effects vary by language and benchmark. Language-wise random masks can move ASR substantially: in instruction-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-it, from 30.47% to 40.95% in Korean and from 65.71% to 46.03% in Bengali. MESA reports benchmark-dependent specificity, including large random-mask effects on Qwen Strata. Frontier refusal estimates, and some significance judgments, differ between rule-based and model judges.

method_sensitivity.factor: Sparsity threshold, module selection and output quality
method_sensitivity.what: NeuRel's threshold sweep (model and aggregation unspecified; no matched baseline) peaks at its selected similarity threshold 0.85, with 100% ASR on MaliciousInstruct, against 72% at 1.00 and 8% at 0.38. Effectiveness does not simply rise with parameter budget. TwinBreak on LLaMA 2 7B (HarmBench) gives 49% ASR with Up-only and 17% with Down-only pruning. Adding Down to Gate+Up reaches 96%, with substantial utility loss. In LLaMA-3 8B MLP reweighting, a large sparsity penalty run to convergence (rho=1e-3) gives about 87% ASR (Direct Request 2.5). Under 0.1% of factors fall below 0.9 at T(n-2), layer 13, against under 3% at T(n-1), layer 18 in the main run, and output quality is somewhat worse. Section 4.4 reports that the method works with rho near 0, so no graded sparsity–coherence link is shown. Larger attention-head removals can degrade coherence, which affects whether outputs count as successful harmful responses.

At α=−0.5, safety is 85% for Top-64 heads, 96% for heads ranked 64–128 and 68% for generic safety-related heads, against a 99% baseline. Generic heads give 45% safety at α=−0.6 and 40% at α=−1.0. Table 11 does not explicitly identify the model or benchmark; LLaMA-3-8B is inferred.

method_sensitivity.factor: Model and utility-task condition under NeuroStrike
method_sensitivity.what: Without defense on SST2, ASR is 0.89 for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 0.83 for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 0.81 for Falcon3-7B-Instruct. Llama's GSM8K-task ASR is 0.91. The pruned fraction is unspecified, and no random-pruning control establishes selection specificity.

status_amendment.public_note: The status now says that its study counts were compiled before the source checks, and it names the studies that still contest specific readings of the claim after those checks. It also adds a new result of this kind, a mixture-of-experts pruning test (Qwen1.5-MoE) where pruning did not raise attack success, and the level stays R2.
